label: Q3 2026 (Jul–Sep)
asOf: close of $483.90 on 3 Nov 2026 (Investing.com); about +7% after hours
headline: Data center doubles and Q4 guidance is $17B: AMD's AI accelerators are finally ramping, but the stock already ran a long way ahead

points.b: MI450 and Helios start to ramp
points.t: Data center revenue rose 27% q/q with record GPU and CPU sales; Q4 guidance of $17B is $3.6B more than this quarter, mostly from Helios racks.

points.b: Gross margin isn't rising with it
points.t: Non-GAAP gross margin of 56%, guided down to 55% for Q4: full racks include more bought-in parts, so the price is higher but the margin lower.
Free cash flow was only $554M; inventory rose from $7.9B at the start of the year to $11.5B to prepare Q4 shipments, and new debt took total debt from $3.2B to $7.1B.

reaction: Stock: closed at $483.90 (+3.7%) on report day and rose about 7% after hours (Investing.com). Revenue, EPS and Q4 guidance all beat. The stock has more than doubled this year, but fell 17.5% in October with the AI trade (the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index fell 15.4%), from a high of $649.42 on 6 Oct. Next day (4 Nov) it closed at $488.78, +1.0%, against −2.7% for the semiconductor ETF (SMH). 4 Nov was the first day after the midterms, when the AI chain split: cloud companies rose while power, cooling and construction stocks fell hard. Consensus from Investing.com: EPS $1.94, revenue $13.06B, Q4 revenue $16.23B.

segments.title: Revenue mix
segments.take: All of the increase came from data center; console chips fell in a generation lull, while PCs and embedded grew modestly.

rows.why: Instinct MI450 GPUs began shipping and EPYC server CPUs hit a record. Operating profit $2.88B at a 34% margin, against 25% a year ago. The first Helios racks are running at customers including Meta, Microsoft, OpenAI and Oracle.
Ryzen notebook processors drove the y/y growth; down 4% q/q.
Console custom chips and discrete graphics both fell, with consoles in the trough before a new generation.
Recovery across aerospace and defense, auto, communications and industrial. Operating profit $453M, a 41% margin.

segments.note: Client and gaming are reported as one segment, with combined operating profit of $573M ($867M a year ago). “All other” (stock compensation, amortization and so on) lost $1.08B and is not allocated to segments.

extras.title: Where it sits in the AI loop
extras.take: AMD is the loop's second AI accelerator supplier: cloud companies and AI labs buy its GPUs and full racks to train and run models, paid for out of their capex. It is also the second-largest server CPU supplier, and AI agents need plenty of CPUs alongside GPUs.

items.w: Helios puts 72 MI450 GPUs, EPYC CPUs and NICs into one rack, competing head on with NVIDIA's NVL72. The price is higher, but more bought-in parts dilute the margin.

items.b: Big customers locked in multi-year demand
items.w: This year it signed a multi-year 6 GW agreement with Meta (reported at about $60B), and last year a 6 GW agreement with OpenAI that included warrants. Fair-value changes on those warrants cut GAAP profit by $1.1B this quarter.
AI inference and agent workloads need more general-purpose compute, and Oracle, Google Cloud and Microsoft are all launching new EPYC instances. CPUs are AMD's most distinctive advantage over NVIDIA.

items.b: Software is still the weak spot
items.w: ROCm 10 shipped, but the developer ecosystem still trails NVIDIA's CUDA. AMD is filling gaps with acquisitions: this quarter it announced World Labs (model research) and Taalas (inference silicon).

items.b: Dependent on a few customers' capex
items.w: Data center growth is concentrated in a handful of cloud companies and AI labs. If they slow capex or shift more to in-house chips (Google TPU, Amazon Trainium, Broadcom custom silicon), AMD's growth feels it first.

extras.title: Where growth comes from
extras.take: AMD's growth rests almost entirely on how much data center GPU share it wins: Q4 guidance means quarterly revenue goes from $9.2B to $17B in a year. The questions are how long that pace lasts and whether margins hold.

items.w: Q4 revenue rises $3.6B q/q, mostly Helios. MI450 ships for the full year next year, then MI500.
Full racks carry a lower margin than chips alone. Whether it gets back above 57% at scale decides whether profit can grow faster than revenue.
Non-GAAP operating margin rose from 24% to 29%: opex grew 29% while revenue grew 45%.
November 2025 analyst day: revenue growth above 35% a year over 3–5 years, data center above 60%, EPS above $20. It is ahead of that pace so far.
Helios delivery delays; big customers delaying deployments; HBM memory and advanced packaging (CoWoS) shortages; export controls; NVIDIA cutting Rubin prices to defend share.

trends.why: Doubled in a year, +27% q/q in Q3
Q4 guidance is another big step up
Stocking up cut this quarter's cash flow to $554M

valuation.take: About 73 times trailing non-GAAP earnings and about 61 times 2026, with a P/S of about 18, more than twice its five-year median of about 8. The market is already pricing profits from 2028 on: if growth holds, the multiple falls fast; if it slows, the downside is large.

forward.title: Full-year 2026 from company guidance
steps: Q4: $17B revenue × 55% gross margin − about $3.9B opex, 13% tax, 1.665B shares ≈ $2.85
forward.note: Q4 EPS is our estimate from guidance; the company gives no EPS guidance. Opex is this quarter's $3.56B plus 10%.

scenarios.note: Bear: AI capex slows in 2027 and revenue stalls at Q4's annualized level; base: close to the analyst-day targets, with data center still growing fast; bull: a clearly larger GPU share. EPS = revenue × non-GAAP operating margin × (1 − 13% tax) ÷ 1.68B shares (including warrant dilution). These assumptions are ours and are not forecasts.

pricezone.sub: 2028 EPS × our P/E; price at the 3 Nov close (before the report)
pricezone.why: The price is far above the zone: buying at $484, the base case gains only about 18% and the bear case loses about 48%, a reward/risk of about 0.4. At the $365 top of the zone the reward/risk is about 1.9; at the $330 low end, about 3.2. The base case already assumes AMD gets close to its long-term targets, and 30x is above most chip companies; today's price is roughly paying for an outcome between base and bull. After hours it was about $518, further from the zone.

history.title: Against its own past 5 years
history.sub: P/S (TTM revenue, diluted shares), quarter ends
history.note: About 18x now, more than twice the five-year median of about 8x; it reached 22–23x in June and at end-September. We use P/S because GAAP profit is depressed by Xilinx amortization and the warrants, which distorts GAAP P/E. We calculate it from SEC quarterly revenue, diluted shares and quarter-end closes.

cash.title: Cash generation
cash.note: Free cash flow of $554M this quarter, after $2.57B and $1.56B in the prior two: inventory is $3.5B above the start of the year and receivables $2.9B higher, stocking up for Q4 rack shipments; capex was $648M against $258M a year ago. New notes issued in August took debt from $3.2B to $7.1B.
